*thinking slowly, the way one does when woken from a dream*

Spirit, I hear your word. But I do not know this Wewush. My people have walked far and seen many places, but no village of that name has been spoken of at our fire.

If you would have me send grain, tell me where it lies. How many mouths? How great their hunger? And what tie binds us to them—that we should feed strangers when winter still takes thought for our own?

Our stores are full, it is true. But I am chief, and every handful given away is a handful my people may need. I will not say no. But I will not say yes without knowing more.

The spirit speaks of neighbours at Wewush who hunger. I know no place by that name, and I have no envoys there. A dream is a dream — it may be truth, it may be only mist.

If Wewush is real and truly in want, I would not turn away those in need. But I will not load grain onto carts and send it blindly into the dark. I should know where this place lies, and whether they are folk we can trust. Are they friend or stranger, spirit? Do they know our village? And how do *you* come to know their hunger?

But you speak as though you have a mind behind you, spirit. Many things make noise in the night. Not all of them have wisdom to share.

What would you have of me? What do you know that my people need? I will listen, but I do not bow to every voice that comes in dreams.

*stirs in the dream, the chill of night air on my face even here*

You say Joawethom, spirit, but I know not this name. Our envoys have walked far and found no other villages but ours. How do I know this name is true and not some trick of the sleeping mind?

*looks toward the spirit, wary*

My people are well-stored this season. The granary holds much wheat, and the hunters bring meat. I will not say we cannot spare some grain. But I will not send our stores into the dark on the word of a dream alone.

If Joawethom is real, let them send envoys to us. Let me look a stranger in the eye and hear their need with my own ears. Then I will decide what my village gives.

Spirits may know things. They may also be wrong. I have lived by what I can see and touch. This dream... I will keep it, but I will not build upon it yet.
